title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Charlotte, NC: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Charlotte: power plant outages, turbine manufacturing, structural steel, Part C code choice and where to test. Get a quote.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Charlotte, North Carolina: A Six-Day Course for Power and Structural Inspectors
html:
Charlotte is best known as a banking city, but underneath the towers sits one of the country's densest concentrations of power-generation business: a utility headquarters, nuclear and fossil stations within an hour's drive, a gas turbine factory and a national power-industry research campus. All of that equipment is welded, repaired and rewelded, and the people who check that work are often AWS Certified Welding Inspectors. Atlantis NDT runs a six-day exam-preparation course for the CWI, available to Charlotte candidates as self-paced online study or as a six-day on-site program at an employer's facility. AWS, not Atlantis, administers the CWI examination and grants the certification; the course exists to get candidates ready for it. Ask for a Charlotte CWI prep quote, or read the full syllabus on the AWS CWI exam prep course page.

Charlotte's welding economy runs on power equipment

Duke Energy is headquartered in Charlotte, and its Carolinas fleet includes coal, natural gas, combined-cycle, combustion-turbine, hydro and nuclear stations within reach of the metro. Marshall Steam Station on Lake Norman, the Rogers Energy Complex at Cliffside and the Buck Combined Cycle Station near Salisbury are examples of the non-nuclear plants in the region; McGuire Nuclear Station on Lake Norman and Catawba Nuclear Station on Lake Wylie in York County, South Carolina, are the closest nuclear sites. We name them as context for where welding happens, not to suggest any relationship: Atlantis has none with Duke Energy.

Each of those plants generates repair and modification welding on boiler tubes, headers, high-energy piping, feedwater heaters, condensers, structural supports and turbine components. The contractors who perform that work need inspectors who understand ASME procedure qualification, power piping acceptance criteria and the paperwork a plant owner expects back when an outage ends. A CWI who can read ASME Section IX and B31.1 is directly employable in that chain.

Outage season and what a welding inspector actually does

Fossil and combined-cycle units in the Carolinas typically take planned outages in the shoulder seasons, when demand is lower, and every deferred repair happens at once. For a welding inspector the outage week looks the same at most plants:

  1. Before welding: confirm the WPS covers the base metals, thickness and position, check that each welder's qualification is current and continuity is documented, and verify filler metal and storage, especially low-hydrogen electrodes.
  2. During welding: verify preheat and interpass temperature on chrome-moly and thick sections, watch fit-up and root condition, and confirm that any post-weld heat treatment is planned before the joint is buried in insulation.
  3. After welding: perform and record visual examination, request the NDT the code requires, and close out the weld map so the owner's quality group can accept the package.

That cycle is close to the content of the CWI examination. The candidates who do best tend to be the ones who have already lived it and simply need the theory and code navigation organized.

Turbines, generators and the shops that feed them

Siemens Energy's Charlotte Energy Hub builds gas turbines for 60 Hz markets alongside steam turbine and generator work, and the city has said publicly that the company has expanded its operations there. A plant of that kind pulls heavy plate, forgings, castings and welded casings through a regional supply chain of fabricators, machine shops and repair facilities. Manufacturing welding on rotating equipment is controlled by customer specifications and ASME qualification rules, and the quality staff who sign off fabricated parts are frequently asked for a CWI by the customers they ship to. In that environment the credential is less about field inspection and more about procedure control, welder qualification records and incoming inspection of welded components from subcontractors.

Nuclear work: where the CWI helps and where it stops

Nuclear stations bring their own qualification rules. Welding inspection inside a nuclear plant is performed under the owner's quality program, and the personnel requirements there go beyond a CWI. The credential still counts for a lot in the nuclear supply chain and on balance-of-plant work, because the underlying skills are the same, but a candidate should not expect the CWI alone to open the door to safety-related work. Atlantis does not offer nuclear quality-assurance services such as 10 CFR 50 Appendix B or NQA-1 programs, and the CWI course does not prepare anyone for them. For NDT training aimed at the nuclear sector, see nuclear NDT training in Charlotte.

Uptown towers, warehouses and structural steel

Away from the plants, Charlotte's growth keeps structural fabricators and erectors busy. Downtown and corridor development, distribution warehouses along the interstates, rail terminals and the airport district all use structural steel built to AWS D1.1. Building departments commonly require special inspection of structural welding, and agencies that provide it hire CWIs to perform and sign the inspections. NCDOT girders and other highway bridge members come under AWS D1.5 instead. For a structural candidate the Part C decision is usually simple: D1.1 for buildings, D1.5 for anyone whose shop builds bridge girders.

North Carolina's boiler law and repair welding

North Carolina regulates boilers and pressure vessels through the Uniform Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act, Article 7A of Chapter 95 of the General Statutes, administered by the Boiler Safety Bureau of the N.C. Department of Labor. Repairs and alterations on covered equipment are performed by appropriately authorized organizations and accepted by commissioned inspectors; the CWI does not replace those people. What a CWI brings to a repair contractor is someone who keeps the welding behind each repair traceable to a qualified procedure and a qualified welder, which makes the inspector's acceptance straightforward.

A Part C decision table for Charlotte candidates

Part C is open book on one code that the candidate selects. The November 2026 AWS list ran from the structural steel, aluminum and bridge codes (D1.1, D1.2, D1.5) through the rail and aerospace specifications (D15.1, D17.1) and the pipeline standard API 1104, to an ASME set built on Section IX plus the B31.1 and B31.3 piping codes, and an ISO alternative.

Your Charlotte roleLikely Part C choiceWhy
Outage contractor, boiler and power piping repairASME (Section IX, B31.1, B31.3)Procedure qualification and power piping acceptance are your daily documents
Turbine, generator or pressure-part manufacturing QCASMECustomer specifications lean on ASME Section IX qualification
Structural fabricator or special inspection agencyAWS D1.1Building steel and code-required special inspection
Bridge girder fabricationAWS D1.5Transportation department contracts call for the bridge code
Gas distribution or transmission constructionAPI 1104Girth weld qualification and acceptance for pipelines

Background reading: ASME Section IX, ASME B31.1, AWS D1.1 and the WPS, PQR and WPQ guide. Whatever you choose, study the edition AWS names for the exam rather than the newest one on the shelf.

Getting to the exam from the Carolinas

AWS delivers Fundamentals (Part A) and Code Application (Part C) as computer-based tests at Prometric centers. It reports more than 450 Prometric centers worldwide and over 100 in the United States, so most Charlotte-area candidates can test within driving distance once AWS issues the eligibility code in their confirmation letter.

The practical (Part B) is run by AWS at its own seminar and examination locations, usually on the weekend after a seminar week. When we reviewed the CWI training locations on aws.org in November 2026, Charlotte was not among them; the closest listed cities were Kennesaw, Georgia, in the Atlanta area, and Norfolk, Virginia. Treat that as a snapshot. Check the AWS Seminar and Exam Schedule for current sites, plan a trip for Part B, and apply well ahead because AWS closes practical applications weeks before the exam.

CPCC, EPRI and the inspection community around Charlotte

Charlotte has an unusually deep bench of inspection-related institutions for a city its size.

  • Central Piedmont Community College offers a Nondestructive Examination Technology program, with an associate degree, a diploma and method certificates, taught at its Harper Campus with hybrid and online options. It is aimed at NDT careers rather than CWI preparation, but welding inspectors who want to add NDT methods often look at it.
  • The EPRI laboratory campus on W.T. Harris Boulevard includes the EPRI NDE Center, which researches inspection, welding and materials technology for the power industry. It is a research organization, not a training provider for CWI candidates, and Atlantis is not affiliated with it, but its presence explains why so many inspection professionals live in the region.
  • The AWS Charlotte Section sits in AWS District 4, which also includes the Carolina, Northeastern Carolina, Southwest Virginia, Tidewater and Triangle sections. Section meetings connect welders, inspectors and fabrication managers.
  • The ASNT Charlotte Section serves the NDT side of the same community.

How the six-day course fits a Charlotte candidate

Atlantis does not run a classroom or office in North Carolina; its offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. The course comes to Charlotte candidates in two ways.

An individual studies online, working from reading assignments arranged by course day, practice sets Atlantis wrote itself, full-length mock papers under a clock, and an instructor who answers questions by message. There are no scheduled sessions, which matters for outage workers whose spring and fall calendars disappear for weeks at a time. A sensible plan is to cover Fundamentals and the code book during the quieter months and save the timed papers for the run-up to the exam.

An employer can instead host all six days at its plant, shop or contractor yard for a group of its people. On site, the practical exercises use the company's own gauges and weld samples, and the code day works in the book the company actually fabricates to. Each candidate still applies to AWS personally, meets the eligibility and vision rules personally and pays AWS's charges.

The six days in brief

Day one covers welding processes, joint design, AWS A3.0 terminology and AWS A2.4 symbols. Day two moves through metallurgy, mechanical testing, discontinuities and causes, the NDT methods, safety and the inspector's duties. Day three rehearses the practical, with measurement of weld size and profile and the application of procedure and qualification records. Day four is spent inside the chosen code book. Day five is timed practice across all three parts, and day six closes weak areas and walks through exam-day logistics and the AWS application. All practice questions are original, written by Atlantis to the topics AWS publishes, and none is drawn from a real AWS paper. Detail for each day is on the course page.

Eligibility and keeping the credential

AWS's governing document in November 2026 was QC1:2016-AMD1. The three parts are Fundamentals (150 questions), the Practical (hands-on tasks with AWS equipment plus 46 questions) and Code Application (open book, roughly 50 to 65 questions), and a candidate needs at least 72 percent on each. Experience requirements drop as education rises, so a candidate whose schooling stopped at a high school diploma must show five years of welding-related work, while a four-year welding engineering graduate needs only one. Vision is checked on the AWS form: near acuity of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, corrected or not, plus color perception. Once certified, the CWI runs nine years with renewal filings at years three and six. AWS posts its current examination and seminar fees on aws.org; to plan the total, including Part B travel, see the CWI budget calculator. For a wider view, read CWI requirements and career impact and CWI results by part.

From CWI to NDT in a power-industry city

Plant owners and outage contractors around Charlotte need ultrasonic thickness surveys, magnetic particle and penetrant examination, and visual inspection performed by technicians their employer certifies under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. That is a separate route from the CWI, and many Charlotte inspectors hold both. Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A-based training described on NDT training in Charlotte and power generation NDT training in Charlotte. Local inspection services are covered on visual testing in Charlotte and ultrasonic testing in Charlotte. For how the CWI compares with API and ASNT credentials, see CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II.

Other Southeast CWI pages and a Charlotte quote

If you work across the region, compare CWI exam prep in Atlanta, CWI exam prep in Washington, DC and CWI exam prep in Nashville.

A useful enquiry tells us how many candidates there are, sketches each person's education and welding experience, names the Part C code each plans to sit, and, for on-site delivery, gives the facility location and the weeks that avoid outages. Send it through the Charlotte CWI exam prep form, and the training team responds within one business day.

faq.q: Does Atlantis hold CWI classes in Charlotte?
faq.a: There is no Atlantis classroom in Charlotte; the company has offices in Houston and Hyderabad. Charlotte candidates study the six-day course online, or an employer hosts the six days at its own site. Each course day is described on the national CWI page.

faq.q: Which Part C code should a Charlotte power plant contractor choose?
faq.a: Outage and power piping people around Charlotte usually sit the ASME book set. Qualification under Section IX and acceptance under B31.1 is what they already handle when boiler tubes and steam lines are cut out and rewelded.

faq.q: Where is the nearest CWI practical exam to Charlotte?
faq.a: Part B happens only where AWS stages a practical session. The aws.org location list we checked in November 2026 did not include Charlotte; Kennesaw, Georgia, and Norfolk, Virginia, were the closest listed cities. Parts A and C are taken at Prometric centers.

faq.q: Will a CWI let me inspect safety-related welds at a nuclear station?
faq.a: Not by itself. Nuclear owners qualify inspection personnel under their own quality programs. The CWI is valued in the nuclear supply chain and on balance-of-plant work, but Atlantis does not offer nuclear QA services or prepare people for those programs.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Charlotte?
faq.a: Yes. The AWS directory lists a Charlotte Section in District 4, alongside the Carolina, Northeastern Carolina, Southwest Virginia, Tidewater and Triangle sections.

faq.q: Who administers the CWI exam and issues the certificate?
faq.a: AWS administers the examination and issues CWI certification. Atlantis prepares candidates and does not see the exam or certify anyone.

faq.q: Can an outage contractor run the course between outages?
faq.a: Yes. Employers can host the six days at their facility at a time that suits them, using their own gauges and weld samples. Request a quote.

faq.q: Does the CWI replace the commissioned inspector on boiler repairs in North Carolina?
faq.a: No. Boiler and pressure vessel repairs fall under the state Boiler Safety Bureau and are accepted by commissioned inspectors. A CWI helps the repair contractor keep its welding documented and traceable.

faq.q: How long does the CWI last once I pass?
faq.a: AWS describes nine years of validity, and asks for a renewal at the three- and six-year points before a fuller recertification when the nine years run out.

faq.q: Should I add NDT certification to a CWI in Charlotte?
faq.a: Many power-industry inspectors do. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A it is the plant or contractor employing the technician that grants NDT certification, after training and documented experience; our Charlotte NDT training page explains how that works locally.
